newsitem.title: TURKEY: Arafat calls for international pressure on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat calls for international pressure on Israel.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat called on international backers of the Middle East peace process to force Israel to abide by the accords it has signed, amid a row over Jewish settlements in Arab East Jerusalem.

"I am looking for the the co-sponsors, America and Russia, the European Union and those who signed the agreement in the White House to protect the peace which they have signed," Arafat told Turkish television channel TRT in an interview, broadcast on Thursday.
"Patience has limits," said Arafat, on a one day visit to Ankara for meetings with Turkish officials.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged on Wednesday to build 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa, a hill of pine trees between Jerusalem and Bethlehem captured by Israel in the 1967 war.

Critics say the plan would spark Palestinian rage that could prove more costly than gun battles in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died last year after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
Arafat accused Israel of laying a "siege they are insisting on following up against the Palestinian people" and breaking accords establishing Palestinian self-rule.
Arafat and assassinated Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin signed a peace deal at the White House in 1995 that expanded on a framework accord they had initialled in Washington in 1993.

The PLO wants Arab East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state and has called Israeli housing projects an attempt to cement the Jewish state's hold over all of the city. Israel views all of Jerusalem as its capital.
Arafat was to meet Turkish President Suleyman Demirel and Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for talks on Turkey's contribution to the peace process later on Thursday.
Turkey last week sent 17 soldiers to the West Bank town of Hebron as part of a multinational monitoring force.
